title: Multi-Dimensional Sidebar: progressive reveal, pinned dashboards, and task-scoped lanes for workspace switching
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: As teams grow usage of Redwood Console for ops (rollouts, cost monitoring, per-route tracing) the current left rail feels flat: navigation mixes long-lived entities (projects, models, dedicated pools) with workflow/stateful surfaces (live rollouts, active dashboards). Switching context across workspaces and workflows is slower than it should be and causes duplicated app state and mental overhead.

Proposal: Introduce a multi-dimensional sidebar that surfaces three progressive lanes: 1) Global workspace scope (workspaces and account-level settings), 2) Workspace context lanes (projects, dedicated pools, model catalog), and 3) Task-scoped lanes (pinned dashboards, active rollouts, live traces). The sidebar progressively reveals lanes as users drill in and supports fast workspace switching via a compact selector at the top and a hover-preview microcard for lanes.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce average time-to-switch-workspace by 30% for power users (tracked by product event 'nav.workspace_switch_time').
- Increase discoverability of pinned dashboards by 25% (tracked by 'ui.open_pinned_dashboard').
- Preserve / improve 508 accessibility score; ensure keyboard-first traversal and screen reader labels for lane boundaries.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Single unified rail vs multi-lane rail: unified rail reduces visual complexity but forces deep vertical lists. Multi-lane adds visual affordance cost but enables immediate scope isolation and contextual pinning. We favored multi-lane to improve state separation and reduce accidental cross-workspace actions.
- Progressive reveal animations vs instant reveal: animations help orientation but can feel slow under high-interaction scenarios. Decided on reduced-motion friendly 120ms reveal with user preference respect.
- Compact workspace selector (top) vs global switcher modal: compact selector is lower friction for frequent switches; modal retained as fallback for long lists and keyboard search.

Prototype links and artifacts:
- Figma prototype (high-fidelity): https://redwood.design/figma/console-sidebar-proto-55123 (contains keyboard flows, hover preview microcards, and pinned dashboard interactions)
- Clickable flow recording: https://redwood.record/flows/DES-55123-sidebar-flow.mp4
- Sketches and IA matrix: https://drive.redwood/team/design/ia-sidebar-matrix-2026-02.pdf
- PRD reference: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Sidebar+Multi-Lane+PRD

Review feedback summary (from 2026-02-20 design review):
- PM (Leah Park): positive on reducing mental load; asked for clearer delineation when a lane contains cross-workspace objects. Action: add lane-level header with workspace badge and 'scope lock' affordance.
- Eng (Ravi Patel): concerned about runtime cost of hover microcards and render complexity on low-end devices. Action: provide lazy-loading microcards and a static preview fallback.
- Research (Jordan Lee): requested A/B test variants for compact selector vs modal for >20 workspaces. Action: include analytics hooks and gating flags.
- Accessibility (Priya Desai): flagged missing ARIA live regions for lane reveal and ambiguous alt text for pinned dashboard thumbnails. Action: update prototype with aria-expanded, aria-controls and descriptive alt copy.

Open questions to resolve before handoff:
- Permitted actions in task-scoped lanes: should users be allowed to create new resources (e.g., start a rollout) from a pinned dashboard microcard? (Options: quick action only vs full create modal).
- Autosave behavior for per-workspace filters: when switching lanes, should filters persist across workspaces?
- Default pinning rules: which dashboards should be auto-suggested for pinning (recently opened, frequent-errors, cost-spike alerts)?

Acceptance criteria (design):
1) Figma prototype includes keyboard-first flows for lane navigation and workspace search.
2) Interactive hover microcard implemented with lazy load placeholder state.
3) Documentation for new analytics events and A/B test variants committed to PRD.
4) Accessibility checklist complete and validated by accessibility reviewer.
5) Design tokens/specs exported and annotated for engineering handoff.

Engineering notes for handoff (summary):
- Prefer CSS-based transitions with reduced-motion media query support.
- Microcards should fetch minimal data: title (string), status tag, last-updated (relative), and small thumbnail URL. Fetch on hover with 200ms debounce; fallback to static skeleton.
- Provide a UI toggle for 'compact workspace selector' that falls back to modal when workspace count > 25.
- Add telemetry events: nav.workspace_switch, nav.lane_open, nav.pin_toggle, ui.microcard_fetch, ui.microcard_render_time.

Next steps and timeline:
- 2026-02-22: iterate prototype with accessibility changes (Aisha) — DONE

- 2026-03-02: design review with PM and Research; update PRD with analytics hooks — IN PROGRESS
- 2026-03-08: final handoff bundle to ENG for alpha build (target)
